item.title: US judge steps aside in dispute over Hawaii energy settlement
item.description: A federal judge in Hawaii has disqualified himself from hearing a dispute over whether a decades-old price-fixing settlement bars the state from suing Chevron and other energy companies over climate change, concluding that he has a potential conflict of interest as a Hawaiian resident.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: A federal judge in Hawaii has disqualified himself from hearing a dispute over whether a decades-old price-fixing settlement bars the state from suing Chevron and other energy companies over climate change, concluding that he has a potential conflict of interest as a Hawaiian resident. In an order on Tuesday , US District Judge Micah Smith withdrew from further participation in the litigation, leading the court's chief judge to assign Oregon-based US District Judge Michael Mosman to take over. Smith, who joined the bench in 2023, said he and members of his family lived in Hawaii during the 1990s and might qualify as parties covered by the statewide settlement. “This conflict almost certainly extends, in one way or another, to all other district judges in the District of Hawai'i,” Smith wrote. Smith did not immediately respond to a request for comment left with his office. Chevron did not immediately respond to a request for comment, and Hawaii referred to its court submissions. In court filings, Chevron and Hawaii said they saw no need for Smith to recuse himself. The underlying lawsuit, filed by the state in 1998 on behalf of Hawaii residents, accused a group of energy companies of price-fixing and deceptive marketing. The case later settled for $35 million. Chevron and the other defendants denied wrongdoing. Earlier this year, Chevron and the other defendants asked Smith to enforce the settlement by blocking Hawaii from pursuing certain climate-related claims alleging the deceptive manufacturing, marketing and sale of petroleum products. The companies contend the settlement bars the related litigation that Hawaii is pursuing in state court. Before issuing his recusal ruling, Smith asked the Judicial Conference of the United States' Committee on Codes of Conduct for ethics guidance. The committee told Smith that because the case was brought on behalf of Hawaii residents under a federal antitrust statute, the judge and his wife have a "financial interest in the subject matter" of the action. But the committee said there were steps he could take to avoid recusal. Smith said he could not avoid the conflict of interest because he had already spent a substantial amount of time on the matter and because obtaining ethics waivers would be impractical. The case is Anzai v. Chevron Corp, US District Court for the District of Hawaii, No. 1:98-cv-00792. item.title: Trading Day: US yields cross 5% threshold
item.description: US bond yields soared on Wednesday, in many cases to the highest since 2007, and expectations of an interest rate hike next month surged, after figures showed that US business activity is expanding at its fastest pace in more than five years.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded:
US bond yields soared on Wednesday, in many cases to the highest since 2007, and [USN:S0N4490DT TEXT:"expectations"] of an interest rate hike next month surged, after figures showed that US [USN:ZON00GJOX TEXT:"business activity"] is expanding at its fastest pace in more than five years. The sharp rise in market borrowing costs, and higher oil prices, pushed [USN:L6N45F0EX TEXT:"stocks"] into the red. In [USN:L6N45E0W6 TEXT:"my column today"], I look at the risk to ordinary investors posed by the record concentration of US stock market value in AI and 'tech-adjacent' companies. Passively managed index tracker funds are essentially tech funds now. Today's Key Reads [USN:L1N45F09P TEXT:"Pezeshkian says Iran won't surrender, after Trump's annihilation threat "] [USN:ZON00GJOX TEXT:"US business activity at more than five-year high; inflation pressures building"] [USN:L6N45915R TEXT:"There's a reason Trump is the only one talking about 1% interest rates"] Darkest before dawn? Funds mull return to bonds: Mike Dolan [USN:L6N45E0T3 TEXT:"Trump's diesel export dilemma — Good politics, bad economics: Bousso"] Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: Wall Street down: Dow -0.7%, S&P 500 -0.8%, Nasdaq -1.1%. [USN:L4N45F0EL TEXT:"Europe"] -0.4%. SECTORS/SHARES: Every sector on the S&P 500 falls except energy, which rises 1%. Comms services, utilities -2%. Expedia, Airbnb -8%. Booking Holdings, McDonald's -5%. Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike Holdings +5%. FX: [USN:L4N45F01K TEXT:"Dollar"] leaps 0.5% to highest in nearly 2 months. Dollar/yen above 158.00. BONDS: French 10y 4.60%, US 10y 5.10%, highest since 2007-08. Extremely weak US 5y auction - lowest demand since 2018. COMMODITIES/METALS: [USN:L4N45F015 TEXT:"Oil"] snaps 5-day losing streak, Brent +4%, WTI +2%. [USN:L6N45F0ZY TEXT:"US diesel"] futures -2% to 2-week low. [USN:L4N45F01C TEXT:"Gold"] -1.5%.

Today's Talking Points: 'Risk free' 5% The yield on every US Treasury note or bond, with the exception of the two-year note, traded [USN:L8N45E1BK TEXT:"above 5%"] on Wednesday, with the five-year yield crossing that threshold for the first time since 2007. The two-year yield is only 5 basis points away, so it's conceivable that the whole US Treasury yield curve could be above 5% later this week. That would also be a first since 2007. It's only a number, but it could have psychological significance. It could tempt all kinds of investors to diversify away from expensive stocks and lock in attractive returns on 'risk-free' assets (the real yield on 10-year TIPS is 2.78%, the highest since 2008). On the other hand, today's 5-year auction was awful. These yields are a reminder that we are in a brave new world, where the cost of capital is high and seemingly heading higher. Debt servicing — for consumers, businesses and the Treasury — is getting more expensive. Buckle up. Here Xi comes Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in Washington for his summit on Thursday with US President Donald Trump . The visit will be marked with [USN:L6N45E02J TEXT:"pomp, pageantry and platitudes"], but will it yield much else? Investors' expectations are low, but Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent indicated on Wednesday that there may be some [USN:S0N43U01A TEXT:"progress on trade."] Bessent said the US is open to extending the trade truce that expires on November 10 or considering a possibly larger trade deal, without giving details, other than it was the Chinese delegation's proposal. If Trump and Xi reach agreement on trade, there's unlikely to be much [USN:L6N45C084 TEXT:"cooperation on AI"]. Mutual trust is low, and neither side wants to slow down development. Diesel down US diesel futures slid 2% on Wednesday to a two-week low, reacting to comments from Trump the day before that he backs a ban on US diesel exports as a way to cool record high prices at the pump. Politico also reported that the administration was preparing a 90-day ban, which a White House official denied. Confused? Trump will no doubt be desperate to get diesel prices down, especially ahead of the US midterm elections in November . But while an export ban might play well politically, it [USN:L6N45E11V TEXT:"may not have the desired effect"], as it could push US refineries to cut the amount of crude they process, which would reduce the amount of gasoline and other products produced, which could raise prices. item.title: Burnham backs lifting restrictions on alcohol at English soccer matches
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is considering allowing fans to drink alcohol while watching men's soccer live in England on a trial basis, arguing that the four-decade-old restrictions are outdated and unfairly discriminate against fans of the sport.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Piper
item.content:encoded: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is considering allowing fans to drink alcohol while watching men's soccer live in England on a trial basis, arguing that the four-decade-old restrictions are outdated and unfairly discriminate against fans of the sport. The consumption of alcohol in the stands of the top five tiers of English men's soccer has been banned since 1985, when fighting between rival fans at matches was common. Fans are allowed to drink alcohol when they are away from the pitch. "I think that legislation dates to an era where football was very different," Burnham, a lifelong soccer fan, told reporters travelling with him to New York for this week's [USN:L8N45E1DL TEXT:"United Nations General Assembly"]. "I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination. There are different ways it could be done. It could happen on a trial basis." Burnham took over the premiership in July from Keir Starmer, vowing to boost the popularity of the ruling Labour Party in the face of a challenge from Nigel Farage's anti-immigration Reform UK, which is popular among blue-collar voters. In response to Burnham's remarks, a spokesperson for the UK Football Policing Unit said alcohol plays a significant role in soccer-related violence and it would be "irresponsible to fuel this" by allowing alcohol consumption during matches. LIMITS ARE A LEGACY OF 1980s SOCCER VIOLENCE The introduction of all-seat stadiums, tougher policing and CCTV surveillance, alongside soccer's commercial transformation, has helped reduce violence at matches since 1985, when 39 people died after fighting broke out before the European Cup final between Liverpool and Juventus at the Heysel Stadium in Belgium. English clubs were banned from European competitions for five years as a result. A trial allowing fans to drink alcohol in view of the pitch was held in the English Women's Super League during the 2025-26 season. A survey of supporters found that 90% said matches remained safe and family friendly. Allowing fans to drink in the stands on a permanent basis would involve changes to the Sporting Events (Control of Alcohol etc.) Act 1985 that would require a parliamentary majority. Burnham, a long-time Everton fan who took [USN:L8N4580S6 TEXT:"Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney"] to a game last week, referred to other sports, such as rugby and cricket, where fans can generally consume alcohol while watching a match live. "I don't see how it can be fair that some supporters of one sport can be treated differently," he said. The spokesperson for the UK Football Policing Unit said soccer experiences levels of violence not seen in other sports, and it would be "incredibly rash" to make any fundamental changes without a thorough review of the evidence and talks with the police. Across Europe, there are different approaches to allowing fans to drink alcohol at soccer matches. While German fans can buy and drink beer in the stands during games, Spain and France are among countries that maintain restrictions on alcohol sales at stadiums.

item.title: Peso mexicano rebasa las 17.50/dlr en víspera decisión Banxico
item.description: El peso mexicano se depreció el miércoles a niveles por encima de 17.50 por dólar, presionado por un fortalecimiento global de la divisa estadounidense y la cautela de los inversionistas un día antes de la decisión de política monetaria del Banco de México.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El peso mexicano se depreció el miércoles a niveles por encima de 17.50 por dólar, presionado por un fortalecimiento global de la [USN:L1N45F0TE TEXT:"divisa estadounidense"] y la cautela de los inversionistas un día antes de la decisión de política monetaria del Banco de México. El mercado espera que la autoridad mantenga sin cambios su tasa de interés de referencia el jueves, a medida que crecen las apuestas por nuevas alzas de la [USN:L1N4580OQ TEXT:"Reserva Federal"] de Estados Unidos, un escenario que podría reducir el apetito por activos locales. * La moneda cotizaba en 17.5078 unidades hacia el final de la sesión, con una pérdida de un 1.4%, mientras que el dólar alcanzó su nivel más alto en casi dos meses y los [USN:L1N45F0SY TEXT:"precios del petróleo"] cerraron con un alza cercana al 4%. * "Para la jornada de mañana, el tipo de cambio se enfrenta a una sesión crítica", dijo Felipe Mendoza, analista de mercados de la firma EBC Financial Group "Desde la perspectiva del análisis técnico, se proyecta un rango de fluctuación comprendido entre 17.32 y 17.68", agregó. * Autoridades de la Fed han señalado esta semana que podría ser necesario un mayor endurecimiento monetario si la inflación no cede con suficiente rapidez. El gobernador [USN:L6N45F0SK TEXT:"Michael Barr"] se sumó el miércoles a esos comentarios al decir que probablemente se tendría que aplicar nuevas alzas de tasas de interés. * A su vez, el jefe de la Fed de Chicago, [USN:L6N45F0YG TEXT:"Austan Goolsbee"], advirtió que el reciente avance de los precios del petróleo podría convertirse en una fuente persistente de inflación. * Tasas de interés más altas en Estados Unidos reducirían el diferencial con México, que durante años ha respaldado las operaciones de "carry trade", atrayendo flujos hacia activos locales. * La atención de los inversores se centraba por ahora en la decisión del [USN:L6N45D0SW TEXT:"Banco de México"]. Si el organismo prolonga la pausa en su tasa de referencia, como espera el mercado, un menor diferencial frente a Estados Unidos podría restar atractivo a la moneda mexicana. * Los inversionistas se preparan además para un encuentro previsto el jueves entre el presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, y su par chino, [USN:L6N45F08F TEXT:"Xi Jinping"]. * La bolsa mexicana cedió después de dos jornadas al alza, en línea con el desempeño negativo de [USN:L1N45F0V9 TEXT:"Wall Street"]. El índice líder S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) bajó un 0.28%, a 64,276.72 puntos. * Las acciones de la cementera Cemex (CEMEXCPO.MX) encabezaron las pérdidas, con una caída del 3.04%, a 17.23 pesos. Les siguieron los títulos de la minorista Chedraui (CHDRAUIB.MX) que retrocedieron un 1.88%, a 84.18 pesos. * En el mercado secundario de deuda, el rendimiento del bono gubernamental a 10 años terminó la jornada en 9.37%. La tasa a 20 años culminó en 9.80%.

item.title: US FDA plans move to speed up vape, pouch approvals, WSJ reports
item.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is expected to unveil measures in the coming days that would speed up approvals for vaping products and nicotine pouches, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is expected to unveil measures in the coming days that would speed up approvals for vaping products and nicotine pouches, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter. The FDA is expected to announce it will revisit a 2021 rule outlining requirements for new tobacco applications, according to the report. The agency could also simplify requirements for scientific studies and speed up review times to add flexibility for more products to get authorized, the report said. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. The FDA did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Tobacco companies have long urged U.S. President Donald Trump and other key officials for changes including a faster, clearer FDA authorization process. Last month, the FDA [USN:L6N44P0ZU TEXT:"allowed"] the marketing of three new 'JUUL2' e-cigarette products, adding to a series of approvals for nicotine products that the agency says may offer a better alternative to traditional cigarettes. "The Trump administration is committed to keeping nicotine out of the hands of kids, getting counterfeit vaping products off the streets and providing safer alternatives for adults who want to quit smoking cigarettes," a HHS spokeswoman said, according to the WSJ report. During Trump's first term, his administration had moved to pull flavored e-cigarettes from retail shelves as part of a broader effort to curb youth vaping, warning that sweet flavors had enticed millions of children to become addicted to nicotine.

item.title: Zelenskiy alerta Rússia para um inverno doloroso caso negociações para trégua energética fracassem
item.description: O presidente ucraniano Volodymyr Zelenskiy advertiu Moscou na Organização das Nações Unidas nesta quarta-feira que a Ucrânia deve retaliar e tornar o inverno que se aproxima extremamente doloroso para a Rússia, caso as duas partes não consigam chegar a um acordo sobre uma trégua para os ataques a instalações de energia antes que o frio se instale.
item.dc:creator: Tom Balmforth, Antoni Slodkowski, Simon Lewis
item.content:encoded: O presidente ucraniano Volodymyr Zelenskiy advertiu Moscou na Organização das Nações Unidas nesta quarta-feira que a Ucrânia deve retaliar e tornar o inverno que se aproxima extremamente doloroso para a Rússia, caso as duas partes não consigam chegar a um acordo sobre uma trégua para os ataques a instalações de energia antes que o frio se instale. A Ucrânia e seus aliados correm contra o tempo para garantir acordos relacionados à infraestrutura energética e navegação no Mar Negro antes do inverno, temendo novos ataques russos a instalações de energia e aquecimento, enquanto Moscou continua demonstrando pouco interesse em negociações mais amplas para pôr fim à guerra. “Os ucranianos entendem que este inverno pode ser muito rigoroso para nós. Mas, em resposta, não teremos outra escolha a não ser torná-lo doloroso também para a Rússia”, disse Zelenskiy à Assembleia Geral da ONU durante o encontro anual de líderes mundiais em Nova York. Embora a Rússia possua um arsenal de mísseis muito maior, que tem usado para bombardear seu inimigo ao longo da guerra, a Ucrânia desenvolveu e utilizou milhares de drones de longo alcance para contra-atacar armazéns russos, infraestrutura portuária e refinarias de petróleo. “É exatamente por isso que dizemos que são necessárias medidas de distensão antes do inverno”, disse Zelenskiy, pedindo uma diplomacia mais robusta e destacando a influência que o presidente chinês, Xi Jinping, poderia exercer sobre o presidente russo, Vladimir Putin. O ministro das Relações Exteriores da Rússia, Sergei Lavrov, manteve conversas com o secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, nesta quarta-feira. Após o encontro, Rubio afirmou que tanto a Ucrânia quanto a Rússia haviam manifestado interesse em um cessar-fogo limitado envolvendo alvos relacionados a grãos e energia. No entanto, não houve sinal imediato de qualquer mudança na posição russa. Um comunicado do Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Rússia afirmou que, na reunião, o país havia “reafirmado seu compromisso incondicional com a consecução dos objetivos de sua operação militar especial” -- expressão que Moscou usa para descrever sua guerra na Ucrânia. Dirigindo-se aos 15 membros do Conselho de Segurança à margem da reunião anual da ONU com líderes mundiais, Lavrov indicou que Moscou não deve aceitar qualquer cessação temporária das hostilidades. “A Europa, independentemente do que pense, só quer uma pausa e pretende aproveitá-la para abastecer o regime de Kiev com armas”, afirmou em uma sessão do Conselho dedicada à guerra na Ucrânia. Os principais diplomatas do Reino Unido, França e Dinamarca aproveitaram seus discursos para proferir fortes condenações à guerra da Rússia, alertando de diversas maneiras para uma escalada perigosa e o aumento no número de mortes de civis. Zelenskiy aproveitou seu discurso na Assembleia Geral para destacar o papel de Putin como impulsionador da guerra, descrevendo-o repetidamente de forma sarcástica como “paciente zero” e “aquele de quem essa ideia de guerra continua se espalhando cada vez mais”. “É por isso que o ‘paciente zero’ deve ser detido. É preciso negar a ele o espaço para agir -- e o espaço para espalhar ainda mais esse mal”, afirmou. Zelenskiy disse aos líderes, durante cúpula da “Plataforma da Crimeia” realizada paralelamente à ONU, que Kiev está pronta para uma trégua marítima no Mar Negro com base em propostas como as apresentadas pelo Egito, pela Índia e pela Turquia. “Estamos aguardando a resposta da Rússia. A Ucrânia está pronta... para garantir a segurança da navegação e a segurança alimentar no Mar Negro, caso a Rússia também esteja disposta a tomar medidas concretas para a redução da tensão. Temos que começar por algum lugar”, disse. Os principais importadores de trigo na Ásia, no Oriente Médio e na África, que dependem da região do Mar Negro para o abastecimento, têm enfrentado dificuldades para garantir seus suprimentos. Os preços globais do trigo dispararam.

item.title: Turkey and Iraq agree Turkey will turn over military camp in northern Iraq
item.description: Turkey and Iraq agreed on Wednesday for Turkish forces to hand over a military camp in northern Iraq to the Iraqi government gradually, they said after talks in New York, adding they also agreed to end the presence of "outlawed armed elements" in northern Iraq.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Turkey and Iraq agreed on Wednesday for Turkish forces to hand over a military camp in northern Iraq to the Iraqi government gradually, they said after talks in New York, adding they also agreed to end the presence of "outlawed armed elements" in northern Iraq. After Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan met on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, the sides said in a joint statement they had agreed to deepen security cooperation. "Within this framework, they reached an agreement on fully establishing state authority in Sinjar and ending the presence of outlawed foreign armed elements," they said, referring to Kurdish militants, some of whom are based in the mountainous Sinjar area of northern Iraq. Turkey is continuing a [USN:L1N4470U0 TEXT:"peace process"] that it hopes will result in the disarmament of those militants from the outlawed Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) and end a decades-old conflict. The statement on Wednesday added that "in accordance with the agreed-upon mechanism and timeline" and security measures taken by Iraq, Turkish forces would gradually hand over the Bashiqa-Zelikan base, a military installation in northern Iraq near Mosul, to the Iraqi government. An Iraqi military commander familiar with the talks said the phased withdrawal of Turkish troops from the Bashiqa camp and another small base near Mosul was expected to be completed by the end of this year. There was no immediate comment from Turkey on the timeline. Ankara deployed troops near Mosul in 2015, saying they were there to train and protect Iraqi forces and local Sunni Arab, Turkmen and Kurdish fighters preparing to fight Islamic State, which seized Mosul in 2014. The deployment sparked a dispute with Baghdad, which demanded the troops’ withdrawal, while Ankara said they were supporting the anti-Islamic State training mission. Turkey still has several bases in the region, which it says are there to protect Turkey's national security. Tom Barrack, US ambassador to Turkey and special envoy for Syria and Iraq, welcomed the move, saying "Iraqi sovereignty and Turkish security, both (were) served" by it. The joint statement said the two leaders also discussed bilateral ties and trade, stressing the need to urgently implement [USN:L6N43Y034 TEXT:"previously signed agreements"] and speed up "strategic projects."

item.title: Popular celebrity golf tourney staying in Tahoe through 2030
item.description: The annual celebrity golf tournament that draws scores of professional athletes and entertainers will remain at its current Lake Tahoe home in the Sierra Nevada Mountains through 2030.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The annual celebrity golf tournament that draws scores of professional athletes and entertainers will remain at its current Lake Tahoe home in the Sierra Nevada Mountains through 2030. The American Century Championship has agreed to a four-year extension to keep the tournament at Edgewood Tahoe Golf Course in Stateline, Nev., along the border of California. Former professional tennis player Mardy Fish won the 2026 edition of the tournament in a field that included the Golden State Warriors' Stephen Curry, former NBA star and current broadcaster Charles Barkley, former Philadelphia Eagles lineman Jason Kelce and longtime NHL star Joe Pavelski. In 2025, Pavelski won the celebrity tournament title after Fish won the second of his three titles in 2024. Curry won in 2023, while former Dallas Cowboys quarterback and broadcaster Tony Romo won in 2018, 2019 and 2022. The last non-athlete to win the tournament was actor Jack Wagner in 2011. The event, held on the weekend of the second full week of July, has been played in South Lake Tahoe every year since it made its debut in 1990. Stateline is home to four casino resorts: Bally's, Caesars, Harrah's and the Golden Nugget. The next event is July 7-11, 2027. --Field Level Media

item.title: Australia PM Albanese says OpenAI agent breached government website in June
item.description: Australia Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Wednesday an AI agent developed by OpenAI infiltrated an Australian government website in June, accessing public and non-public files.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Wednesday an AI agent developed by OpenAI infiltrated an Australian government website in June, accessing public and non-public files. "This incident occurred in June this year, and involved an OpenAI agent gaining unauthorized access into the public-facing Medicare Statistics Reporting Service portal, which is administered by Services Australia," Albanese told reporters in New York in remarks broadcast by Australian media. No personal information is believed to have been accessed at this stage but investigations are ongoing, Albanese said, adding that spoke with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman to express "Australia's extreme concern about this incident".

item.title: Kane considers NFL kicking career after soccer
item.description: England captain Harry Kane said on Wednesday he is considering a future as an NFL kicker later in his career, with a possible spell in Major League Soccer potentially helping him make the transition.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: England captain Harry Kane said on Wednesday he is considering a future as an NFL kicker later in his career, with a possible spell in Major League Soccer potentially helping him make the transition. Kane had previously expressed his interest in pursuing careers in golf and American football. Now the 33-year-old is giving more serious thought to a future in the NFL, though he stressed any potential move to the United States is still several years away. "That is something I will try and look at a bit more seriously," Kane told reporters at England's training camp. "It all depends on what happens in my career over the next five or six years. The NFL is a lot more realistic than the golf one, let's put it that way." The Bayern Munich striker said his penalty-taking experience could give him a head start as an NFL kicker, though switching sports would take serious preparation. "I take penalties and it is a very similar pressure and technique," he said. "In terms of training, I would be closer to that more than any other sport. "But, with all elite sports, when you watch it on TV, people make it look easy; you think it is possible, but that is not always the case. "If I was to do it, it is something I would take seriously. I would take maybe six months to a year of trying to practice before." Kane also suggested a move to MLS could provide a way to combine the two sports. "Maybe if I am in the MLS in the future or somewhere like that it might be a thing where you could connect the two maybe with the seasons," he said. There are already examples of soccer players making the switch. Dallas Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey was a first-round MLS draft pick by Toronto FC in 2017 but never made an official appearance for the first team. Jake Bates also played college soccer before becoming a kicker for the Detroit Lions. Kane's immediate future, however, remains in soccer, with talks over a new contract at Bundesliga champions Bayern progressing and an announcement expected soon. "We're in good talks," Kane said. "There's still some things that we need to iron out. I'm happy there. I think it won't be too long before there's some sort of announcement."

item.title: Vídeo em que “candidato” orienta compra de votos é sátira
item.description: Um vídeo em que um suposto candidato a deputado explica como comprar votos no primeiro turno das eleições de outubro circula nas redes sociais como se fosse verídico, mas se trata de um conteúdo de humor.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Um vídeo em que um suposto candidato a deputado explica como comprar votos no primeiro turno das eleições de outubro circula nas redes sociais como se fosse verídico, mas se trata de um conteúdo de humor. Aqui estão os principais detalhes: No vídeo , que circula no Facebook e no Threads, o suposto candidato afirma que irá transferir dinheiro vivo para funcionários e que eles têm até as 17h do dia 4 de outubro, data do primeiro turno, para “estar zerados de dinheiro, comprar o máximo de voto que vocês puderem”. O vídeo foi publicado originalmente nos perfis de um humorista amazonense conhecido como Raipado , que é o homem que aparece nas imagens. Em seu perfil no Instagram, ele se apresenta como criador de conteúdo de humor e sátiras políticas. Raipado não é deputado estadual nem federal pelo Estado. O humorista já fez vídeos similares anteriormente, que também foram alvo de desinformação . Veredicto: Sátira. Trata-se de um vídeo de humor, e não verídico, um material sobre compra de votos. item.title: Wells Fargo's chief risk officer Derek Flowers to retire
item.description: Wells Fargo said on Wednesday its chief risk officer, Derek Flowers, would retire in mid-January after nearly three decades at the US banking giant.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Wells Fargo (WFC.N) said on Wednesday its chief risk officer, Derek Flowers, would retire in mid-January after nearly three decades at the US banking giant. Flowers, who started at Wells Fargo in 1995, held various roles at the fourth-largest US bank. He has been the chief risk officer since 2022 and will be succeeded by Chief Operating Officer Scott Powell. "Derek played a pivotal role in strengthening our risk and control framework and fostering the strong risk culture that positions Wells Fargo for continued growth," CEO Charlie Scharf said. Wells Fargo plans to name Powell's successor in the near future.

item.title: Trigo tem menor valor em 4 semanas em Chicago por negociações diplomáticas na Ucrânia
item.description: Os contratos futuros de trigo ampliaram sua queda para o menor nível em quatro semanas na bolsa de Chicago (CBOT) nesta quarta-feira, diante das expectativas de que os esforços diplomáticos possam amenizar as interrupções nas exportações do Mar Negro relacionadas à guerra entre a Rússia e a Ucrânia, segundo analistas.
item.dc:creator: Tom Polansek
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros de trigo ampliaram sua queda para o menor nível em quatro semanas na bolsa de Chicago (CBOT) nesta quarta-feira, diante das expectativas de que os esforços diplomáticos possam amenizar as interrupções nas exportações do Mar Negro relacionadas à guerra entre a Rússia e a Ucrânia, segundo analistas. Os futuros do milho e da soja também caíram. A Ucrânia e a Rússia, ambos grandes fornecedores de grãos, manifestaram interesse em um cessar-fogo limitado envolvendo alvos relacionados a grãos e energia, afirmou o secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, após se reunir com o ministro das Relações Exteriores da Rússia, Sergei Lavrov, em Nova York. Operadores do mercado afirmaram que uma trégua poderia levar à retomada do transporte de cargas, que está praticamente paralisado no Mar Negro, afetando os embarques de grãos russos e ucranianos. As vendas técnicas também pesaram sobre os futuros, que recuaram após atingirem uma máxima em três anos neste mês, segundo analistas. "O trigo é o mais atrasado no mercado de grãos, possivelmente mudando sua tendência de alta para uma de baixa, à medida que o suporte técnico está sendo rompido", disse Brian Hoops, presidente da Midwest Market Solutions. O contrato mais negociado de trigo fechou em queda de 8,75 centavos, a US$7,085 por bushel. O presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, se reuniu com o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, na terça-feira e afirmou que eles discutiram um cessar-fogo em alvos relacionados à energia. Os futuros de milho e soja recuaram após se aproximarem de máximas de três anos nesta semana, com os operadores aguardando para ver se a cúpula EUA-China na quinta-feira impulsionará a demanda chinesa por safras americanas. A China é o maior importador mundial de soja. "As negociações prévias com os chineses não deram nenhuma indicação de que algum acordo sobre grãos seja anunciado", afirmou a corretora Marex em uma nota. O milho fechou em queda de 7,75 centavos, a US$5,29 por bushel, enquanto a soja caiu 7,50 centavos, para US$13,18 por bushel.

item.title: TCU recomenda ao governo análise de alternativas à caducidade no caso da Enel SP
item.description: O plenário do Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) aprovou nesta quarta-feira uma recomendação para que o Ministério de Minas e Energia e a agência reguladora Aneel estudem alternativas à caducidade no caso da distribuidora Enel São Paulo, a fim de que sejam avaliados os impactos que a medida teria aos consumidores de energia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O plenário do Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) aprovou nesta quarta-feira uma recomendação para que o Ministério de Minas e Energia e a agência reguladora Aneel estudem alternativas à caducidade no caso da distribuidora Enel São Paulo, a fim de que sejam avaliados os impactos que a medida teria aos consumidores de energia. No processo, relatado pelo ministro Augusto Nardes, ficou recomendado que, antes de uma eventual declaração de caducidade da concessão da distribuidora da Enel, o governo e a Aneel façam uma "análise estruturada" dos efeitos dessa extinção contratual. Essa análise deverá contemplar, pelo menos, operadores aptos a assumir a concessão, cronograma de transição operacional, custo de indenização dos bens reversíveis, impacto tarifário esperado e risco sistêmico para o setor de distribuição, "demonstrando, de forma fundamentada, que a caducidade produz benefício líquido ao consumidor", diz o acórdão. A sugestão aprovada pelo TCU está alinhada ao [USN:L1N44V0JK TEXT:"pedido formulado pela Enel à Aneel"], nas alegações finais da empresa no processo de caducidade que tramita no órgão regulador. Segundo a companhia de energia italiana, a Aneel precisa considerar as consequências "práticas" da caducidade -- a penalidade mais severa que pode ser aplicada a uma concessionária --, algo que ainda não teria sido feito no processo até agora. A Enel busca reverter a conclusão da Aneel de que sua distribuidora paulista apresenta "falhas estruturais" na prestação dos serviços, com base no desempenho da empresa para restabelecer a energia a seus clientes após eventos climáticos extremos em 2023, 2024 e 2025. A diretoria da Aneel ainda decidirá se recomenda ou não a caducidade da concessão da Enel São Paulo ao Ministério de Minas e Energia, que tem a palavra final sobre o tema. A caducidade nunca foi aplicada a um contrato de concessão de distribuição de energia elétrica no Brasil. Em casos anteriores, os operadores ou passaram por intervenção do poder público, que assumiu os serviços, ou decidiram vender a concessão. A deliberação da Corte de Contas ocorreu em processo aberto em 2023, por representação formulada pelo Ministério Público junto ao TCU, para que o órgão analisasse as causas do blecaute ocorrido na época na área de concessão da Enel e acompanhesse as medidas adotadas pelo governo federal sobre o caso. Também ficou determinado no processo que o governo e a Aneel terão que enviar ao TCU, no prazo de 60 dias, "cronograma detalhado" das ações previstas para garantir a adequada continuidade da distribuição de energia em São Paulo após o término do contrato atual da Enel São Paulo, em 2028. A empresa italiana buscava renovar antecipadamente sua concessão paulista, mas isso está em suspenso até que haja uma conclusão sobre o processo de caducidade.

item.title: AI firms should not get regulatory waivers, Nvidia CEO says on podcast
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang believes AI firms should not receive exemptions from antitrust or liability laws, according to a podcast released on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Nellis
item.content:encoded: Nvidia (NVDA.O) CEO Jensen Huang believes AI firms should not receive exemptions from antitrust or liability laws, according to a podcast released on Wednesday. In a nearly two-hour interview with New York Times podcast host Ezra Klein, Huang, CEO of the world's most valuable publicly listed company, had an extensive discussion about OpenAI agents that [USN:L6N44N119 TEXT:"hacked Hugging Face"], the open-source AI software hub that [USN:L4N44V0WH TEXT:"Nvidia purchased for $13 billion this month"]. Huang, who has [USN:FWN4560E8 TEXT:"opposed blanket AI safety regulation"] even as labs such as OpenAI and Anthropic [USN:L6N4511GE TEXT:"have called for it"], reiterated his position that it is the responsibility of AI labs to test their products and only release models once they are satisfied models are safe. "However, in the complexity of the work that they do, to ask for regulatory relief for antitrust or product liability relief — that I don’t think makes sense. When you’re asking for regulation, don’t ask for relief of the current ones," Huang said, according to a transcript published by the newspaper. In an essay published this month, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for an antitrust waiver allowing AI labs to work together on safety issues. Some U.S. officials such as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have said AI firms have asked for liability shields, without naming specific firms. In other portions of the interview, Nvidia's Huang said that he is not opposed to regulations for specific products where AI is applied, such as self-driving cars. "The car as a product — the robo-taxi — has lots of regulations. If it doesn’t have enough regulations, then NHTSA ought to get involved and come up with new regulations," Huang said. "The car industry should have new regulations. I don’t know what’s missing, but if there is something missing, then I would absolutely add more regulation."

item.title: Maior mina de cobre do mundo suspende operações após a morte de trabalhador
item.description: As operações na maior mina de cobre do mundo, a mina Escondida da BHP , no Chile, foram suspensas nesta quarta-feira após a morte de um trabalhador em um acidente, informou a empresa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: As operações na maior mina de cobre do mundo, a mina Escondida da BHP (BHP.AX) , no Chile, foram suspensas nesta quarta-feira após a morte de um trabalhador em um acidente, informou a empresa. A BHP informou que o trabalhador morreu enquanto realizava trabalhos de manutenção. O sindicato que representa os trabalhadores da mina havia informado anteriormente à Reuters que o acidente envolveu uma carregadeira frontal frequentemente utilizada no setor. “Todas as atividades operacionais na mina foram suspensas”, afirmou a BHP em comunicado, sem fornecer um prazo para o possível reinício das operações. Normalmente, no Chile, as minas só podem retomar as atividades após um incidente fatal após inspetores verificarem que as condições são seguras o suficiente. A Escondida está localizada no Deserto de Atacama, no Chile. A BHP opera a mina, enquanto a Rio Tinto (RIO.L) detém uma participação de 30% e a JECO Corp, com sede no Japão, 12,5%. A BHP havia estimado que a mina produziria até 1,28 milhão de toneladas métricas do metal neste ano.

item.title: Café arábica sobe após mínima de 3 meses na bolsa ICE
item.description: Os contratos futuros de café arábica na ICE fecharam em alta nesta quarta-feira, após terem caído anteriormente para a menor cotação em três meses, enquanto os preços do açúcar bruto e do cacau também subiram.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros de café arábica na ICE fecharam em alta nesta quarta-feira, após terem caído anteriormente para a menor cotação em três meses, enquanto os preços do açúcar bruto e do cacau também subiram. CAFÉ * O café arábica fechou com alta de 3,6 centavos, ou 1,3%, a US$2,759 por libra-peso, recuperando-se da mínima de US$ 2,6975. * Os corretores afirmaram que os estoques certificados na bolsa continuam muito baixos, apesar de um aumento modesto nos últimos dias. * Os estoques estavam em 254.480 sacas na quarta-feira, acima da mínima de 27 anos de 217.646 sacas registrada há uma semana. No mesmo período do ano passado, os estoques estavam em 643.341 sacas. Há apenas cerca de 18.000 sacas aguardando recomendação. * Também houve rumores no mercado sobre o tempo seco na América Central, embora as perspectivas para a safra do próximo ano no Brasil, principal produtor, continuem, em geral, favoráveis. * O café robusta subiu 1,7%, para US$3.317 por tonelada métrica, após cair para US$3.218, a menor cotação em três meses e meio. AÇÚCAR * O açúcar bruto fechou em alta de 0,16 centavo, ou 0,9%, a 17,75 centavos por libra-peso, seu terceiro ganho consecutivo. * Corretores afirmaram que as usinas do centro-sul do Brasil se concentraram nesta safra em utilizar a cana para produzir etanol como biocombustível, em vez de açúcar, o que ajudou a reduzir a oferta do adoçante. * A corretora StoneX reduziu, nesta quarta-feira, sua projeção de excedente de oferta de açúcar para a safra que termina em setembro de 2,9 milhões de toneladas para 1,45 milhão de toneladas métricas, citando atrasos na colheita brasileira e menor teor de açúcar na cana. * A perspectiva de menor produção em países asiáticos como Índia e Tailândia, devido ao fenômeno climático El Niño, também ajuda a sustentar o mercado. * O contrato futuro de açúcar branco recuou 0,4%, para US$ 506,00 por tonelada. CACAU * O cacau de Londres fechou com alta de £130, ou 3,3%, a £4.128 por tonelada. * Os corretores afirmaram que as condições de seca na Costa do Marfim, principal produtora, aumentaram as preocupações com as perspectivas para a produção de 2026/27, embora um grande excedente global em 2025/26 tenha garantido que os estoques de curto prazo continuem abundantes. * A produção de cacau de Gana para a safra 2025/26 atingiu cerca de 771.000 toneladas métricas, superando a previsão inicial do órgão regulador, de 650.000 toneladas, de acordo com um relatório analisado pela Reuters na quarta-feira. * O preço do cacau na Bolsa de Nova York subiu 2,3%, para US$ 5.528 por tonelada. (Reportagem de Nigel Hunt e Marcelo Teixeira)

item.title: Petróleo fecha em alta de quase 4%, enquanto presidente do Irã promete nunca se render
item.description: Os preços do petróleo fecharam com alta de pouco menos de 4% por barril nesta quarta-feira, em um pregão volátil, enquanto os operadores avaliavam a promessa do presidente iraniano Masoud Pezeshkian de nunca se render, um dia depois de o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, ter advertido que poderia "aniquilar" o Irã.
item.dc:creator: Georgina Mccartney
item.content:encoded: Os preços do petróleo fecharam com alta de pouco menos de 4% por barril nesta quarta-feira, em um pregão volátil, enquanto os operadores avaliavam a promessa do presidente iraniano Masoud Pezeshkian de nunca se render, um dia depois de o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, ter advertido que poderia "aniquilar" o Irã. Os contratos futuros do petróleo Brent fecharam com alta de US$3,83, ou 3,86%, a US$103,08 por barril, enquanto os contratos futuros do West Texas Intermediate subiram US$ 1,64, ou 1,81%, para US$92,16. Os futuros do diesel com teor ultrabaixo de enxofre caíram cerca de 5% depois que o site Politico noticiou que o governo Trump estava preparando planos para uma proibição de 90 dias à exportação de diesel, notícia que a Casa Branca negou posteriormente. O secretário de Energia dos EUA, Chris Wright, havia afirmado na quarta-feira que uma proibição à exportação de diesel não funcionaria. Analistas e observadores do mercado alertaram que tal medida pouco contribuiria para aliviar os altos preços da energia e poderia agravar a escassez global de suprimentos e perturbar ainda mais as economias. O que impulsionou a alta dos preços do petróleo foi o discurso de Pezeshkian na Assembleia Geral da ONU, em Nova York, em que ele afirmou na quarta-feira que Teerã nunca se renderia aos EUA, mas ainda acredita na diplomacia. Na terça-feira, Trump aproveitou um discurso no mesmo fórum para fazer sua ameaça. Teerã estava analisando a resposta dos EUA à sua proposta de pôr fim às hostilidades, embora ainda haja muitas divergências, disse uma alta autoridade iraniana à Reuters. A reabertura do Estreito de Ormuz e o fim do bloqueio naval de Washington ao Irã foram discutidos durante negociações indiretas na terça-feira, disse a autoridade. Na manhã desta quarta-feira, o chefe de segurança do Irã, Mohsen Rezaei, afirmou que o Estreito de Ormuz não seria reaberto enquanto as condições do Irã não fossem atendidas. Em outros lugares, os estoques de petróleo dos EUA aumentaram em 3 milhões de barris, para 426,4 milhões de barris, na semana encerrada em 18 de setembro, informou a Administração de Informações sobre Energia. Analistas consultados pela Reuters esperavam uma redução de 641 mil barris. Os estoques de combustível diminuíram.

item.title: Orioles C Samuel Basallo (concussion) on IL, INF Jackson Holliday to have wrist surgery
item.description: The Baltimore Orioles placed rookie catcher Samuel Basallo on the seven-day injured list Wednesday due to a concussion and also announced that infielder Jackson Holliday will have surgery next week on his injured left wrist.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Baltimore Orioles placed rookie catcher Samuel Basallo on the seven-day injured list Wednesday due to a concussion and also announced that infielder Jackson Holliday will have surgery next week on his injured left wrist. The Orioles recalled outfielder Heston Kjerstad from Triple-A Norfolk to replace Basallo on the 28-man active roster. Basallo, 22, last played on Monday, when he took a foul tip off his catcher's mask in the fifth inning and exited in the seventh of the Orioles' 4-3 home win over the Toronto Blue Jays. The move to the injured list is retroactive to Tuesday. "Concussions are so finicky," Orioles manager Craig Albernaz said. "Sometimes, it's immediate, and sometimes, it kind of shows up as the night goes. And luckily, we got Sammy up when we did and the symptoms crept up at night. Obviously, you've seen him walking around the clubhouse. It's a quote-unquote not a severe concussion. But during the test, there were a few boxes that he didn't check." Basallo's season ends with a .222 batting average with 18 home runs and 54 RBIs in 112 games this season. The native of the Dominican Republic also was on the IL from July 20 to Aug. 19 because of right shoulder inflammation. "I think Sammy handled himself extremely well," Albernaz said. "There was a lot of growth with Sammy, especially the behind the scenes, the unseen hours and the prep. ... He's such a smart kid, wants to do everything right, and he's done a great job of navigating that." Holliday last played on Sept. 14, going 2-for-4 with one run scored in a 2-1 win over the host New York Mets. He was placed on the 10-day IL, retroactive to Sept. 15, with left wrist inflammation. He met with a wrist specialist in Baltimore on Saturday and he was diagnosed with a partial tear in the triangular fibrocartilage complex, MLB.com reported. "They've just got to get in there and figure out how severe it is," Holliday said. "It's not completely torn, so that's great. Hopefully, just go in there and clean it up and that'll be that." With a recovery period of about 10 weeks, Holliday and Albernaz hope the 22-year-old will be ready for next spring training. "It's one of those where it's a smaller ligament, so once they get in there, they can make a better assessment," Albernaz said. "But a healthy offseason is always a huge aspect for any player, never mind a young player. But identifying this and getting Jackie out there earlier than later is going to help him have a better offseason." Holliday hit .229 with seven home runs, 30 RBIs and 12 doubles in 98 games. In his first full season in the majors last year, he hit .242 with 17 home runs, 21 doubles and 55 RBIs in 149 games. He suffered a broken hamate bone in his right hand while taking batting practice early in spring training. Holliday began the 2026 season on the IL after undergoing surgery and did not make his season debut until May 19. Baltimore selected Holliday first overall in the 2022 MLB Draft. Kjerstad, 27, batted .211 (4-for-19) in 11 games this season for Baltimore. He batted .289 with 11 homers and 44 RBIs in 79 games for Norfolk. The Orioles picked Kjerstad second overall in the 2020 draft out of the University of Arkansas. --Field Level Media

item.title: Colorado ready to move forward after player dismissals
item.description: Colorado is dealing with distractions as it prepares for its Big 12 Conference opener at Baylor on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Colorado is dealing with distractions as it prepares for its Big 12 Conference opener at Baylor on Saturday. Buffaloes coach Deion Sanders dismissed multiple players after last Saturday's 41-7 loss at Northwestern. He said the moves were not solely performance-related. Instead, it was due to behavior that was detrimental to the team. "Those guys can tell you, I'm the most loving and giving and forgiving man you could ever meet," Sanders told reporters. "But when you start being conduct detrimental to the team, that will set us back. Things that you're doing that you don't care about the team -- you care about you. I have a problem with that." During his weekly show, Sanders provided more insight on his reasoning. "People made a big deal out of last week about us getting rid of a few kids. But it wasn't a team thing. It was just a few knuckleheads," Sanders said. "Every occupation we have, (there's) a few knuckleheads. Don't think it was the team. No. It was a few knuckleheads that I didn't want to poison the team." In addition, Colorado safety Ben Finneseth apologized for his comments about Northwestern's temporary stadium along Lake Michigan that was playing host to its final football game. The school is slated to open a reimagined $862 million Ryan Stadium on Oct. 2 against Penn State. In a video, Finneseth said the temporary stadium "f---ing sucks" and "sounds like a library." Finneseth's apology came at a press conference with Sanders at his side. "It was childish; it was a stupid thing that I said. It won't happen again," Finneseth said. "The way I handled it was horrible. I promise you guys it will not happen again and it'll be much more mature moving forward." The Buffaloes are 2-1 entering Big 12 play. They posted wins over Georgia Tech and Weber State before being clobbered by Northwestern. --Field Level Media

item.title: US Senate confirms aide to Texas governor as federal judge
item.description: A longtime aide to Republican Texas Governor Greg Abbott who served as the state's interim attorney general during Ken Paxton's 2023 impeachment proceedings was confirmed by the US Senate on Wednesday as a federal judge.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: A longtime aide to Republican Texas Governor Greg Abbott who served as the state's interim attorney general during Ken Paxton's 2023 [USN:L8N3AS0BI TEXT:"impeachment proceedings"] was confirmed by the US Senate on Wednesday as a federal judge. The Republican-led Senate voted 50-47 to confirm Angela Colmenero, Abbott's deputy chief of staff, to the position of a life-tenured judge in Houston in the US District Court for the Southern District of Texas. The vote came during a [USN:L1N4500N3 TEXT:"push by the White House"] to secure the confirmation of as many judges as possible before the year's end amid the looming risk that Democrats retake the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections. President Donald Trump has secured the confirmation of 290 of his judicial nominees during his two terms, including three US Supreme Court justices, helping shift the judiciary's ideological balance to the right. In nominating Colmenero to a judgeship, Trump in a May social media post hailed her for doing an "incredible job" as a top aide to Abbott and said she would "always protect our Great Constitution." Colmenero, 47, began working under Abbott in 2009 when he was serving as the attorney general of Texas. After Abbott became governor in 2015, she remained in the attorney general's office under Paxton for three years while serving as the chief of its general litigation division. During her time in the office, she defended a Republican-backed state law requiring photo identification at the ballot box and argued in favor of state redistricting plans facing Voting Rights Act challenges. She also served as lead trial counsel in a lawsuit challenging President Barack Obama's executive action to defer deportation of certain immigrant children and parents who are in the country illegally. She rejoined Abbott as an aide to the governor in 2018, initially as a deputy general counsel before rising to become deputy chief of staff in 2023. In response to written questions from Senate Democrats, Colmenero said that while Abbott was governor, she advised on policies ranging from his [USN:L4N2S20UN TEXT:"banning of COVID-19 mask mandates"] to the [USN:L1N3001HD TEXT:"busing of migrants"] to cities led by Democrats. When Paxton was impeached by the Texas House of Representatives in May 2023 on allegations of corruption, Abbott appointed Colmenero as provisional attorney general, a role she held until the state Senate acquitted him that September. Paxton is now the Republican candidate for a seat in the U.S. Senate. Read more: [USN:L1N4500N3 TEXT:"Trump faces tight timeline to appoint judges as midterms loom"]
